intervals.label: construction of the experiment at the FAIR site
intervals.locator: arXiv:2506.20545 abstract ("under development at the future FAIR facility"); arXiv:2004.11762: FAIR "is under construction"
intervals.note: FAIR sources say FAIR "is under construction"; the 2025 CBM paper calls CBM "a next-generation heavy-ion experiment under development at the future FAIR facility". No source states when CBM construction began; April 2020 is the date of the earliest status paper read (arXiv:2004.11762), whose 2025 first-beam expectation has since slipped, and the 2025 commissioning of SIS100 is scheduled for 2H 2027 (arXiv:2510.14948).
intervals.quote: The Compressed Baryonic Matter (CBM) experiment is a next-generation heavy-ion experiment under development at the future FAIR facility in Darmstadt, Germany.

placements.note: Planned location at the FAIR site (campus-grade point); the detector is not yet operating.
placements.quote: The Compressed Baryonic Matter (CBM) experiment is a next-generation heavy-ion experiment under development at the future FAIR facility in Darmstadt, Germany.

summary.plain: A set of fast, radiation-hard detectors in a magnet that will track and identify particles from heavy-ion collisions at up to ten million interactions per second.
summary.technical: CBM: low-mass radiation-hard detector subsystems for vertexing, tracking, particle identification and event reconstruction with a free-streaming self-triggered readout at up to 10 MHz.

technology.quote: Operating in fixed-target mode with a continuous beam of up to 11 AGeV for heavy ions and 26 GeV for protons, CBM will investigate rare probes such as multi-strange hyperons, hypernuclei, and dileptons
technology.value: Free-streaming, self-triggered readout with radiation-hard, low-mass detectors for vertexing, tracking, particle identification and event characterisation
